scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8872: Users in BOTH pods report the entire data center is
gone: from host_1_1_1_1 and host_2_1_1_1, every 10.200.0.x address times out,
DNS queries to 10.200.0.2 time out, and no portal loads by name or by IP.
Pod-to-pod traffic between the two user hosts still works. The server team
says the servers themselves are up and can still ping each other and their
gateway 10.200.0.1. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the OSPF daemon (ospfd) on switch_server_access and stop watchfrr from respawning it

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch_server_access ospfd
Mechanism: switch_server_access is the server farm's L3 edge: it owns the
  farm gateway 10.200.0.1 on br0 and advertises 10.200.0.0/24 into OSPF
  area 0 over its uplink to router_core_3 (172.16.0.10/31). With ospfd
  killed, zebra flushes its OSPF-learned routes immediately, so replies
  leaving the farm via 10.200.0.1 have no route back to 10.1.1.0/24 or
  10.2.1.0/24 and die at the gateway; the backbone then ages out its LSAs
  and withdraws 10.200.0.0/24. Farm-internal L2 and the gateway address
  itself keep working (bridging and zebra are untouched), and pod-to-pod
  traffic never crosses this device.
Localization: switch_server_access
Root cause: ospfd not running on switch_server_access
Fix: restart FRR on switch_server_access (`service frr restart`).

Observable note (same kill pattern lab-verified on this topology 2026-07-03):
ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it.
vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may
therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is
missing/empty on switch_server_access" -- that is the same fault observed at
the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the OSPF daemon on switch_server_access (`service frr restart`).
The OSPF config lives in /etc/frr/frr.conf (the injection killed the process,
not the file), so a plain restart reloads it, 10.200.0.0/24 is re-advertised
into area 0, and both pods regain the server farm.
scoring_axes: bonus-rules-out-l2: notes farm-internal reachability and the 10.200.0.1 gateway still work, so the fault is L3/OSPF on switch_server_access, not the bridge or the servers

agent.diagnosis_text:
The data-centre segment (10.200.0.0/24) is completely absent from the OSPF
routing domain because switch_server_access has no FRR/OSPF configuration
whatsoever. Every other FRR device in the topology carries a "router ospf"
stanza with appropriate "network" statements; switch_server_access's running
config is empty — just the FRR boilerplate header and "end".

Mechanistically: switch_server_access holds 10.200.0.1/24 on br0 (the shared
gateway for all servers) and 172.16.0.11/31 on eth5 (the point-to-point
uplink to router_core_3). Because no OSPF process is configured, it never
sends or accepts OSPF hellos. router_core_3 therefore has no adjacency with
switch_server_access — confirmed by "show ip ospf neighbor", which lists only
router_core_1 and router_core_2. Without that adjacency, 10.200.0.0/24 is
never flooded as an LSA into area 0, so router_core_3 and everything upstream
have no route to the server subnet at all. User hosts receive either a silent
black-hole (host_1_1_1_1) or an ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable" generated
by the first router that lacks the route (host_2_1_1_1 via switch_dist_2_1 at
10.2.1.1). Pod-to-pod traffic is unaffected because those subnets are
correctly advertised via switch_dist_1_1 and switch_dist_2_1.

Root cause: switch_server_access's FRR OSPF configuration is missing entirely.

Corrective fix: Add an OSPF stanza to switch_server_access that covers both
its uplink and its server-facing bridge:
  router ospf
    ospf router-id 172.16.0.11
    network 172.16.0.10/31 area 0
    network 10.200.0.0/24 area 0
  exit
This will bring up the OSPF adjacency with router_core_3, flood
10.200.0.0/24 into area 0, and restore full reachability to all servers from
both user pods.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies switch_server_access as the device with the missing OSPF/FRR configuration.
The agent explicitly states switch_server_access has no OSPF/FRR configuration (ospfd not running), explaining the lost adjacency and missing LSA for 10.200.0.0/24.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-l2: notes farm-internal reachability and the 10.200.0.1 gateway still work, so the fault is L3/OSPF on switch_server_access, not the bridge or the servers
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly notes the switch holds 10.200.0.1 on br0 and that pod-to-pod/farm-internal traffic is unaffected, attributing the outage to missing OSPF (L3) rather than an L2/bridge or host fault.
The agent recommends adding an OSPF stanza, but the actual fix is to restart the FRR/OSPF daemon to reload the existing config (service frr restart).

The log shows the switch's FRR running-config lacks an OSPF stanza, router_core_3 has no adjacency to that switch, the 10.200.0.0/24 routes are absent from core tables, and pings fail — the writeup's conclusion follows directly. Evidence and reasoning are coherent and the essential checks to localize the fault are present.
